name: navigator.platform
plain: Legacy string naming the OS family such as Win32, MacIntel, Linux x86_64 or iPhone.
meaning: Coarse OS signal that is deprecated but still returned. Often frozen to a fixed value (Win32 on 64-bit Windows, MacIntel on Apple Silicon), so it carries little entropy but reveals spoofed user agents when it disagrees.

access.persistence: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored
access.iframe: Readable from cross-origin iframes too (same values)

fields.name: platform
fields.range: Win32, MacIntel, Linux x86_64, Linux armv81, iPhone, iPad, Android-like strings

story.what_it_is: An old text field naming your operating system family, like Win32 or MacIntel.

marketing.name: Navigator.platform
marketing.pitch: Docs mark it as deprecated and say it should not be used for new features.

story.for_you: You never see it. It still tells a site your system family, but modern browsers often freeze it to a fixed value, so it often says Win32 even on a 64 bit machine.
story.for_makers: Sites use it to show the right download button and keyboard shortcut. It is low value now, so it is mostly used to cross check other signals.

use_cases.example: A download page shows the Windows button for Win32 and the Mac button for MacIntel.
A web app shows Cmd shortcuts on a Mac and Ctrl on Windows.
A browser game picks keyboard hints and fullscreen steps for each system.
A fraud tool flags a visitor whose platform is Linux but whose user agent says iPhone.
A traffic dashboard counts visits by operating system.
An advertiser targets Mac users with a premium offer when the platform says MacIntel.

technical_bounds: Deprecated by spec but not removed
Cannot distinguish Apple Silicon from Intel

linkedin.how: Collected as platform. Read by the LinkedIn APFC fingerprint script (48 features, alleged by BrowserGate, partly confirmed by BleepingComputer).

history.change: Win32 and MacIntel are effectively frozen on 64-bit and ARM systems
